**For most MacBook Airs, 30W is the minimum and 70W is the most useful upper end.**

- **Minimum to charge:** Apple lists 30W as the minimum for the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air ([Apple tech specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **What Apple recommends (2022 or later models):** a 30W adapter (13-inch only), a 35W dual-port, a 67W, or a 70W adapter ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)). The 2018-2021 models use a 30W or 40W Dynamic (60W max) adapter.
- **Fast charging:** you need a 70W or higher USB PD source ([Apple M5 specs](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320), [M4 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
- **What's in the box:** the 13-inch M5 includes a 40W Dynamic adapter with a 60W max. The 13-inch M4 includes 30W or 35W, depending on GPU config.
- **Compatibility:** any USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery works, even if its wattage is higher or lower than Apple's recommendation ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)). For the best experience, match or exceed the recommended wattage.

**Quick pick:**
- Basic charging: 30-45W is enough.
- Faster charging, or you use the laptop heavily while it charges: 70W.
- Travel or multi-device: a 65W multi-port charger works. It's slightly under the 70W fast-charge threshold, so it will charge well but may not fast-charge.

**One option from my search:** the [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2-pack, 2× USB-C + USB-A)](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) is $49.99 on Baseus's US store, per the Dealectric listing ([source](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)). That link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy, at no extra cost to you. It delivers 65W from either USB-C port when used alone, but the laptop port drops to 45W when two or three devices are plugged in. That's still enough for a MacBook Air, just not at full speed. Prices change, so check at checkout.
